newsitem.title: SPAIN: Barea reiterates Spain will meet '97 deficit goal.
newsitem.headline: Barea reiterates Spain will meet '97 deficit goal.

text.p: Spanish Budget Office Director Jose Barea reiterated that Spain would meet its 1997 deficit of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
"There isn't going to be a lot of room to spare but we are going to meet it without too much difficulty," Barea told financial daily Gaceta de los Negocios in an interview published on Monday.
"Revenue forecasts will be met and expenditures are not going to give us a scare," he added.
Barea said his office was working on ways to lower the deficit to 2.5 percent of GDP in 1998, as planned in the government's three-year convergence programme.
"It's not going to be easy because we have to do it while maintaining the fiscal burden constant, in other words, by reducing expenditure," Barea said.
Cuts must be made in the public sector with structural reforms if the convergence programme is to be fulfilled.
"There are two (reforms), state-owned companies and the administration, above all in services such as Social Security," Barea said.

Although the one-year-old conservative government launched a privatisation campaign last year, the problem resides in the loss-making state-owned groups rather than in those that have been or are slated for privatisation.
As a first step, the government will approve a plan this year whereby state holding group SEPI, which groups many state-owned companies, will no longer finance loss-making groups with loans.

"But the problems will take four, six years to resolve -- the time that it takes to make the companies as profitable as can be managed and with the time limits established by the EU to allow Spain to grant subsidies," Barea said.
The Administration, in good part, runs like a 19th century service provider, Barea said.

"Either we undertake this reform or we will again have to reduce public investment. And this is a factor that shouldn't be touched. A good part of our deficit is structural. Now that we are in a good economic situation it is the moment to correct these structural problems and introduce market criteria within the Administration," Barea said.
He added that the tax system must be reformed, in personal income tax, corporate tax and value-added tax, in order to further savings and impede inequalities. Tax deductions must also be reviewed.
